# Municipalities — Intro Deck Template

**The standard concept-deck starting point for the Municipalities vertical.** Brand-, persona-, and posture-resolved from the canonicals — you fill three prospect blanks and generate in `claude.ai/design`. Power-user reps self-serve; the GTM asset team runs it for everyone else.

## Fill these three blanks

- **`{prospect}`** — the org you're pitching, e.g. "City of Frisco, TX"
- **`{contact}`** — who you're sending it to + their role
- **`{angle}`** — pick ONE offer below to anchor the deck

## Offers you can anchor on (this vertical)

- Parks & Infrastructure Bond — posture: knowledge
- Downtown Revitalization — posture: knowledge
- New Leadership — posture: knowledge
- Existing Holiday Program — posture: knowledge
- Tourism & Economic Development — posture: knowledge

> **Posture for this vertical: knowledge.** Educate, don't hard-sell. The deck makes the buyer look smart to their own stakeholders — outcomes that matter to their role, not pricing or a hard CTA.

## Audience (pre-resolved — don't re-derive)

Parks & Recreation Director (Director of Parks & Recreation / Director of Public Lands / Leisure Services Director / Parks & Community Services Director); City Manager / Administrator (City Manager / City Administrator / Chief Administrative Officer); Downtown / Events Manager (Executive Director / Downtown Manager / Special Events Coordinator / BID Executive Director / DDA Executive Director)

## Generate the deck

1. Open a new `claude.ai/design` project **seeded from the _BriteBase — Intro Deck Skeleton_** (so brand + slide structure are inherited). If the skeleton isn't seeded, paste the prompt as-is — it carries the tokens inline.
2. Paste the prompt below, with your three blanks filled.

```
Build an animated intro / concept deck for {prospect} (brite-nites — educational, outcome-focused voice).

Audience: {contact} and their stakeholders — decision-makers in the Municipalities vertical (Parks & Recreation Director; City Manager / Administrator; Downtown / Events Manager).
Angle: {angle} — stance = knowledge. Educate, don't hard-sell. The deck makes the buyer look smart to their own stakeholders — outcomes that matter to their role, not pricing or a hard CTA.
Brand tokens (use exactly): orange #ff4d00 as the only saturated color on a light #efefef / #fbfbfa monochrome base; Geist + Geist Mono + MagdaClean type; the brite·base lockup; 1.5px inset strokes (never 1px solid); Linear-style focus ring; lightbulb + soft orange-glow motif.
Shape: dark #0b0b0b title slide (lockup + animated orange glow) → light content slides (eyebrow + tight display + one supporting line; cards with 1.5px inset strokes) → an optional program/product peek → a dark orange-glow close with a knowledge-appropriate CTA.
Sections: title; the opportunity for {prospect}; what a brite-nites program looks like; outcomes that matter to {contact}; the next step.
Interactivity: keyboard-navigable, one idea per slide, staggered entrance, prefers-reduced-motion respected.

Rules: no fabricated stats, logos, or case studies. Do not include any internal account names or targeting/exclusion notes — this is client-facing.
```

## After generating

- Swap `{prospect}` into the title; optionally drop in a real photo of the prospect (their downtown, campus, venue, etc.).
- Run the **Brand-Consistency Checklist** in the `rapid-asset-design` skill before sharing.
- Export a share link, or hand off to Claude Code to clean up and deploy.
